D1.name: Hiring Readiness Optimization
D1.comparative_analysis: Both plans cover the core technical stack (SQL, Python/Pandas, Power BI, statistics, A/B testing) required for a Product/Marketing Data Analyst. Plan 1 integrates interview prep into each monthly milestone with specific SQL LeetCode targets, behavioral framing, and case study practice woven throughout. Plan 2 front-loads technical learning and defers most interview prep to Weeks 10-12, which is late for a 3-month timeline. Plan 1's portfolio approach is more cohesive — it builds one end-to-end project progressively across all three months, culminating in 2-3 polished GitHub projects with business-framed READMEs. Plan 2 also targets 2 projects but the execution is more fragmented, with Project 1 finalized in Week 8 and Project 2 in Week 10, leaving less polish time. Plan 1 explicitly ties portfolio deliverables to business impact narratives, which is critical for DA roles. Plan 2 provides more granular week-by-week SQL/Python topic breakdowns but lacks the same depth of business storytelling integration.
D1.winner_reason: Plan 1 integrates interview prep and portfolio building progressively across all three months with explicit business-impact framing, whereas Plan 2 defers most interview preparation to the final two weeks.

core_technical_readiness.justification: Covers SQL (window functions, CTEs, optimization), Pandas, NumPy, Power BI with DAX, statistical testing, A/B testing, product/marketing metrics, and conceptual ML — all highly relevant. Depth is appropriate for a CSE graduate. Minor gap: no explicit mention of cohort analysis or funnel SQL patterns by name.

portfolio_project_strength.justification: One primary end-to-end project built progressively across 3 months (e.g., SaaS onboarding funnel), supplemented by 2-3 total polished GitHub projects with professional READMEs and executive summaries. D2.name: Time-Constrained Feasibility
D2.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 explicitly calculates total available hours (216), planned hours (190), and buffer hours (26), and allocates time budgets per month across theory, practice, and project work. This is a strong feasibility signal. Plan 2 provides a daily 3-hour breakdown (1 hour core skill, 1 hour application, 1 hour project/review) which is intuitive but does not track cumulative hours or buffer. Plan 1's monthly hour allocations (72+72+72=216 total, 190 planned) are mathematically sound. However, Plan 1's Month 1 asks users to master advanced SQL, Pandas, NumPy, and Git simultaneously in 4 weeks — moderately ambitious but manageable for a CSE graduate. Plan 2's week-by-week topic sequencing is slightly more granular and avoids stacking too many new concepts in a single week. Both plans are broadly feasible for a CSE graduate; Plan 1 edges ahead on explicit hour tracking and buffer planning.
D2.winner_reason: Plan 1 explicitly tracks total hours, planned hours, and buffer hours with monthly allocations, providing concrete feasibility assurance that Plan 2 lacks.

hour_compliance.justification: 216 total hours available, 190 planned, 26 buffer hours explicitly stated. Monthly allocations sum correctly (72+72+72=216). Hour budget is transparent and well-managed.

D4.name: Market Alignment
D4.comparative_analysis: Both plans cover the globally in-demand skill set for Product/Marketing Data Analyst roles: SQL, Python/Pandas, Power BI, statistical testing, A/B testing, and product/marketing metrics. Plan 1 additionally includes attribution models, customer journey mapping, and conceptual API/ML integration — slightly more advanced domain coverage. Plan 2 includes cohort analysis, customer segmentation, and marketing attribution models in domain reading sections, and adds basic ML (regression, clustering) as an optional differentiator. Both plans align well with what global employers hire for at the graduate level. Neither plan includes emerging tools like dbt, cloud-native analytics (BigQuery, Snowflake), or LLM-assisted analytics, which would be differentiators but are not strictly required for this role level. The plans are roughly equivalent on market alignment, with Plan 1 slightly stronger on business domain depth.
D4.winner_reason: Plan 1 covers attribution models and customer journey mapping more explicitly as technical skills rather than just domain reading, giving slightly stronger market differentiation for product/marketing analyst roles.

D5.name: Strategic Prioritization Quality
D5.comparative_analysis: Both plans follow a broadly correct phasing arc for a DA role: SQL/Python foundation → BI tools + statistics/A/B testing → business storytelling + interview prep. Plan 1's three-month themes (Foundation & Project Kickoff → Insight Generation & Visual Storytelling → Business Impact & Job Hunt Sprint) map cleanly to this arc. Plan 2's phasing is similar but slightly less crisp — it introduces Power BI in Week 4 (Month 1) as a 'refresh' rather than deepening it in Month 2, and defers advanced Power BI (DAX) to Week 7. This creates a minor sequencing inefficiency. Plan 1 prioritizes advanced SQL and Pandas in Month 1 (highest ROI for DA interviews), which is correct. Plan 2 starts SQL from basics in Week 1, which is lower ROI for a CSE graduate. Both plans correctly place job hunt activities in Month 3, though Plan 1 begins LinkedIn optimization in Month 1 which is a smart early action.
D5.winner_reason: Plan 1's phasing arc is cleaner and starts at higher-ROI topics immediately (advanced SQL, not basics), while Plan 2 spends Week 1 on SQL fundamentals that a CSE graduate already knows.

D6.name: Curriculum Structural Depth & Clarity
D6.comparative_analysis: Plan 2 has a significant structural advantage in week-by-week granularity — each week specifies exact SQL commands, Python methods, and statistical concepts to learn, along with specific resources (LeetCode, DataCamp courses, specific books). This level of actionable detail makes it easier for a self-directed learner to execute. Plan 1 organizes by monthly themes with weekly micro-goals, which are motivating but less operationally specific — for example, 'Master Pandas GroupBy, Merging, Missing Data handling' without specifying which DataCamp course or documentation section to use. Plan 1's milestone deliverables are stronger and more business-oriented, but Plan 2's subtopic detail is more actionable for daily execution. Both plans have logical module ordering. Plan 2's learning outcomes per week are clearer in terms of what specific skills will be acquired, while Plan 1's outcomes are framed more as portfolio deliverables.
D6.winner_reason: Plan 2 provides significantly more granular week-by-week subtopic detail with specific resources, commands, and methods named, making it more actionable for daily self-directed learning.
